content.body:
Noam Rosenthal: after investigating https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12574, I think the provided test there is not good enough to actually prove the race condition in the spec, I think we just by sheer luck trigger it in chrome and gecko (but its harder for me to reason about chrome actually racing there).

However, in [inner navigate event firing algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#inner-navigate-event-firing-algorithm:~:text=If%20destination%27s%20entry%20is%20non%2Dnull) we seem to just YOLO, if `If destination's entry is non-null:` - but we don't handle null case. And I think the null case *is* the spec race bug. In gecko we're adding what effectively amounts to [what is done here in chrome](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/navigation_api/navigation_api.cc;l=786-794?q=!keys_to_indices_.&ss=chromium%2Fchromium%2Fsrc).

So *maybe* by spec'ing in the null-case there, would solve this. Maybe.
